questions.question: Which ancient civilization created the Code of Hammurabi?
questions.explanation: Babylonian is correct because the Code of Hammurabi was issued by Hammurabi, king of Babylon, in the 18th century BCE.

questions.question: What type of writing was used by the ancient Sumerians?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform is correct because the Sumerians developed this wedge-shaped writing system in ancient Mesopotamia.

questions.question: Which ancient Egyptian ruler commissioned the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.explanation: Khufu is correct because the Great Pyramid of Giza was built as his tomb during the Fourth Dynasty.

questions.question: Which city was destroyed and buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE?
questions.explanation: Pompeii is correct because the eruption of Mount Vesuvius buried the Roman city in 79 CE.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang is correct because he unified China in 221 BCE and founded the Qin dynasty.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek city-state was famous for its military society?
questions.explanation: Sparta is correct because its society was organized around rigorous military training and discipline.

questions.question: Which language appears alongside Egyptian hieroglyphs on the Rosetta Stone?
questions.explanation: Ancient Greek is correct because the Rosetta Stone contains the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Ancient Greek scripts.

questions.question: Which Roman structure was used for gladiatorial contests?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum is correct because this Roman amphitheater hosted gladiatorial contests and other public spectacles.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the city of Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: The Inca is correct because Machu Picchu was built in the Andes by the Inca civilization.

questions.question: Which document was sealed by King John of England in 1215?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta is correct because King John sealed it at Runnymede in 1215.

questions.question: What was the capital of the Byzantine Empire?
questions.explanation: Constantinople is correct because it was the capital of the Byzantine Empire from its foundation as the imperial capital in 330 CE until 1453.

questions.question: Which ruler founded the Mongol Empire?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan is correct because he united Mongol tribes and founded the Mongol Empire in 1206.

questions.question: Which West African ruler made a famous pilgrimage to Mecca in the 14th century?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa is correct because the ruler of the Mali Empire made a renowned pilgrimage to Mecca during the 14th century.

questions.question: Which city was the capital of the Aztec Empire?
questions.explanation: Tenochtitlan is correct because it was the capital of the Aztec Empire, built on an island in Lake Texcoco.

questions.question: Which medieval document records the Norman conquest of England in embroidered scenes?
questions.explanation: The Bayeux Tapestry is correct because it depicts events leading to and including the Norman conquest of England.

questions.question: Which medieval English king ordered the compilation of the Domesday Book?
questions.explanation: William the Conqueror is correct because he ordered the Domesday survey and its record was compiled in 1086.

questions.question: Which city was the center of the medieval Khmer Empire?
questions.explanation: Angkor is correct because it was the capital and major urban center of the Khmer Empire.

questions.question: Which medieval Japanese warrior class served feudal lords?
questions.explanation: Samurai is correct because samurai were the warrior class who served Japan's feudal lords.

questions.question: Which treaty formally ended World War I between Germany and the principal Allied powers?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919 and established the postwar settlement with Germany after World War I.

questions.question: What was the official name of the United States program that provided economic aid to Western Europe after World War II?
questions.explanation: The European Recovery Program was the official name of the Marshall Plan, which aided Western European reconstruction after World War II.

questions.question: Where was the first meeting of the League of Nations Assembly held in 1920?
questions.explanation: The first meeting of the League of Nations Assembly was held in Geneva, Switzerland, in 1920.

questions.question: The Suez Crisis of 1956 followed which country's nationalization of the Suez Canal?
questions.explanation: Egypt, under President Gamal Abdel Nasser, nationalized the Suez Canal in 1956, prompting the Suez Crisis.

questions.question: Who proclaimed the establishment of the People's Republic of China on October 1, 1949?
questions.explanation: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China in Beijing on October 1, 1949.

questions.question: Which organization was established by the North Atlantic Treaty in 1949?
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic Treaty established the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, commonly known as NATO, in 1949.

questions.question: Which military alliance was formally dissolved in 1991?
questions.explanation: The Warsaw Pact, the Soviet-led military alliance in Eastern Europe, was formally dissolved in 1991.

questions.question: Which group captured Phnom Penh in April 1975?
questions.explanation: The Khmer Rouge captured Phnom Penh on April 17, 1975, and established Democratic Kampuchea.

questions.question: Which country launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, in 1957?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on October 4, 1957, beginning the space age and intensifying the space race.

questions.question: The D-Day landings of June 6, 1944, took place in which region of France?
questions.explanation: The Allied D-Day invasion landed on the Normandy coast of France on June 6, 1944.

questions.question: Which treaty ended Soviet Russia's participation in World War I?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, signed in 1918, ended Soviet Russia's participation in World War I.

questions.question: In which country was the Bandung Conference held in 1955?
questions.explanation: The Bandung Conference was held in Bandung, Indonesia, in 1955 and brought together representatives of Asian and African countries.

questions.question: Which two countries were the principal parties to the Camp David Accords of 1978?
questions.explanation: The Camp David Accords were agreements between Egypt and Israel reached in 1978 with United States mediation.

questions.question: In which city was the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries founded in 1960?
questions.explanation: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries was founded at a conference in Baghdad in 1960.

questions.question: Which new state was created alongside India by the partition of British India in 1947?
questions.explanation: The partition of British India in 1947 created the independent states of India and Pakistan; therefore, the correct answer is Pakistan.

questions.question: The Carnation Revolution of 1974 overthrew the Estado Novo regime in which country?
questions.explanation: The Carnation Revolution occurred in Portugal in 1974 and ended the country's Estado Novo dictatorship.

questions.question: What SI derived unit measures catalytic activity and is defined as one mole of reaction events per second?
questions.explanation: katal (kat) is correct because the katal is the SI derived unit of catalytic activity, equal to mol·s⁻¹.

questions.question: What is the molecular point group of an ideal tetrahedral methane molecule?
questions.explanation: T_d is correct because methane has four equivalent vertices arranged tetrahedrally, with tetrahedral symmetry including improper rotations but no inversion center.

questions.question: Why is molecular oxygen, O₂, paramagnetic in its ground electronic state?
questions.correctAnswer: It has two unpaired electrons in degenerate π* antibonding orbitals
incorrectAnswers: It has one unpaired electron in a σ bonding orbital
It has no unpaired electrons because all orbitals are filled
It has two unpaired electrons in σ bonding orbitals
questions.explanation: It has two unpaired electrons in degenerate π* antibonding orbitals is correct because the ground-state molecular orbital configuration of O₂ places one electron in each of two degenerate π* orbitals.

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of iron in the complex ion [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻?
questions.explanation: +2 is correct because six cyanide ligands contribute −6 overall, and the complex charge of −4 requires iron to be in the +2 oxidation state.

questions.question: Which point defect pair characterizes a Schottky defect in an ionic crystal?
questions.correctAnswer: A paired cation vacancy and anion vacancy
incorrectAnswers: An ion displaced into an interstitial site and its vacancy
A substitutional impurity and a dislocation
An electron vacancy and a hole
questions.explanation: A paired cation vacancy and anion vacancy is correct because a Schottky defect consists of charge-balanced vacancies in the crystal lattice.

questions.question: What molecular property must change during a vibrational transition for the vibration to be infrared active?
questions.explanation: Dipole moment is correct because a vibration is infrared active when it produces a change in the molecule's dipole moment.

questions.question: In the nuclear reaction ¹⁰B + n → ⁷Li + ?, what particle completes the balanced reaction?
questions.explanation: ⁴He (an alpha particle) is correct because conservation of mass number and atomic number gives 10 + 1 = 7 + 4 and 5 = 3 + 2.

questions.question: What is the electron configuration of a low-spin octahedral d⁶ metal ion?
questions.explanation: t₂g⁶e_g⁰ is correct because, in a low-spin octahedral d⁶ configuration, electrons pair in the lower-energy t₂g set before occupying the higher-energy e_g set.

questions.question: What is the spin-only magnetic moment of a high-spin d⁵ ion, expressed in Bohr magnetons?
questions.explanation: √35 μB (approximately 5.92 μB) is correct because the spin-only expression is μ = √[n(n + 2)] μB, and a high-spin d⁵ ion has n = 5 unpaired electrons.

questions.question: For a monatomic ideal gas, what is the molar heat capacity at constant volume?
questions.explanation: 3R/2 is correct because a monatomic ideal gas has three translational quadratic degrees of freedom, each contributing R/2 to the molar constant-volume heat capacity.

questions.question: What equation gives the condition for constructive diffraction from parallel crystal planes?
questions.explanation: 2d sin θ = nλ is correct because this is Bragg's law, where d is the interplanar spacing, θ is the Bragg angle, n is an integer, and λ is the wavelength.

questions.question: For a first-order reaction, what is the relationship between its half-life and its rate constant?
questions.explanation: t₁/₂ = ln 2/k is correct because integration of first-order kinetics gives [A] = [A]₀e⁻ᵏᵗ, and setting [A]/[A]₀ = 1/2 yields this relation.

questions.question: What is the ground-state term symbol of atomic carbon, whose valence configuration is 2p²?
questions.explanation: ³P₀ is correct because Hund's rules give the carbon ground term ³P, and for a less-than-half-filled p² subshell the lowest total angular momentum is J = 0.

questions.question: Which thermodynamic quantity is equal to −RT ln K for a reaction at a specified temperature?
questions.correctAnswer: The standard Gibbs energy change, ΔG°
questions.explanation: The standard Gibbs energy change, ΔG° is correct because the equilibrium relation is ΔG° = −RT ln K at the specified temperature.

questions.question: What is the basic structural and functional unit of life?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life because all living organisms are made of one or more cells.

questions.question: Which molecule carries hereditary genetic information in humans?
questions.explanation: DNA carries hereditary genetic information in humans through its sequence of nucleotides.

questions.question: Which organelle is primarily responsible for producing proteins?
questions.explanation: The ribosome is primarily responsible for producing proteins by joining amino acids according to genetic instructions.

questions.question: Which pigment allows plants to absorb light for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll allows plants to absorb light energy used in photosynthesis.

questions.question: What gas do humans normally inhale that is needed for cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is needed for aerobic cellular respiration, which helps cells release energy from food.

questions.question: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces insulin, a hormone that helps regulate blood glucose levels.

questions.question: How many chambers does the normal human heart have?
questions.explanation: Four is correct because the human heart has two atria and two ventricles.

questions.question: Which organ is primarily responsible for exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide with the blood?
questions.explanation: The lungs are primarily responsible for exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body by surface area?
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ of the human body by surface area and forms its external covering.

questions.question: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur is the longest bone in the human body and is located in the thigh.

questions.question: Which part of the human nervous system contains the brain and spinal cord?
questions.explanation: The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord.

questions.question: What type of blood cell transports oxygen using hemoglobin?
questions.explanation: The red blood cell transports oxygen using hemoglobin, the oxygen-binding protein inside it.

questions.question: Which organs filter wastes from the blood and produce urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter wastes and excess water from the blood to produce urine.

questions.question: Which structure connects a muscle to a bone?
questions.explanation: A tendon connects a muscle to a bone and transmits the force of muscle contraction.

questions.question: Which structure connects one bone to another bone at a joint?
questions.explanation: A ligament connects one bone to another bone and helps stabilize a joint.

questions.question: What is the outermost layer of human skin called?
questions.explanation: The epidermis is the outermost layer of human skin.

questions.question: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
questions.explanation: Thymine pairs with adenine in DNA through complementary base pairing.

questions.question: Which process do green plants use to make glucose from light energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.

questions.question: Which organelle contains most of a eukaryotic cell's genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains most of a eukaryotic cell's genetic material in the form of chromosomes.

questions.question: What is the primary function of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: Defending the body against pathogens is the primary function of white blood cells, which are part of the immune system.

questions.question: What is the name of the seismic discontinuity that separates Earth's crust from the mantle?
questions.explanation: Mohorovičić discontinuity is the boundary between Earth's crust and mantle, identified by an abrupt increase in seismic-wave velocities.

questions.question: Which mineral typically crystallizes first from a cooling basaltic magma according to Bowen's reaction series?
questions.explanation: Olivine crystallizes at the highest temperatures in the discontinuous branch of Bowen's reaction series for basaltic magma.

questions.question: The San Andreas Fault is primarily an example of which type of plate boundary?
questions.explanation: Transform boundary is correct because the San Andreas Fault accommodates mainly horizontal motion between the Pacific and North American plates.

questions.question: Karst landscapes most commonly develop through the dissolution of which rock?
questions.explanation: Limestone is correct because slightly acidic groundwater readily dissolves its calcite, forming caves, sinkholes, and other karst features.

questions.question: What is the extrusive igneous-rock equivalent of gabbro?
questions.explanation: Basalt is correct because it has a mafic composition like gabbro but cools rapidly at or near Earth's surface.

questions.question: Which radioactive isotope is commonly used in potassium-argon dating?
questions.explanation: Potassium-40 is correct because it decays to argon-40, allowing potassium-bearing rocks to be dated radiometrically.

questions.question: Where is newly formed oceanic crust generally youngest?
incorrectAnswers: In the center of a passive margin
At the base of a deep ocean trench
questions.explanation: At a mid-ocean ridge is correct because magma rises there and solidifies to create new oceanic crust.

questions.question: What term describes the planar alignment of platy minerals produced during many types of metamorphism?
questions.explanation: Foliation is correct because directed pressure commonly aligns platy or elongated metamorphic minerals into planar fabrics.

questions.question: Which scale is based on the seismic moment of an earthquake and is used to express its magnitude?
questions.explanation: Moment magnitude scale is correct because it calculates earthquake magnitude from seismic moment, which reflects fault area, slip, and rock rigidity.

questions.question: What produces the symmetrical magnetic-stripe pattern on the seafloor on either side of a mid-ocean ridge?
questions.correctAnswer: Seafloor spreading combined with geomagnetic reversals
questions.explanation: Seafloor spreading combined with geomagnetic reversals is correct because newly formed basalt records the alternating polarity of Earth's magnetic field as it moves away from the ridge.

questions.question: Which mineral has a hardness of 1 on the Mohs hardness scale?
questions.explanation: Talc is correct because it is the softest standard mineral on the Mohs hardness scale, assigned a hardness of 1.

questions.question: What type of unconformity places tilted or folded strata beneath younger, more nearly horizontal strata?
questions.explanation: Angular unconformity is correct because it records erosion or nondeposition after older layers were tilted or folded and before younger layers accumulated.

questions.question: Why do many intrusive igneous rocks have relatively coarse crystals?
questions.correctAnswer: They cool slowly beneath Earth's surface
incorrectAnswers: They form only from compressed sediment
They are produced by biological precipitation
questions.explanation: They cool slowly beneath Earth's surface is correct because slow cooling gives crystals time to grow to visible sizes.

questions.question: What is the upper surface of the saturated zone in an unconfined aquifer called?
questions.explanation: Water table is correct because it is the upper boundary of the zone in which groundwater completely fills the connected pore spaces.

questions.question: What geological feature most directly forms where one tectonic plate descends beneath another?
questions.explanation: Subduction trench is correct because the descending plate bends Earth's crust downward, producing a deep oceanic trench at the plate boundary.

questions.question: Which fossil evidence was especially important in supporting the former connection of South America and Africa?
questions.explanation: Mesosaurus fossils on both continents is correct because this freshwater reptile's remains occur in matching-age rocks in South America and Africa.

questions.question: The chemical weathering of feldspar commonly produces which type of secondary mineral?
questions.explanation: Clay mineral is correct because feldspar commonly undergoes hydrolysis during chemical weathering, producing clay minerals such as kaolinite.

questions.question: What cross-sectional shape is most characteristic of a valley carved primarily by alpine glacial erosion?
questions.explanation: U-shaped is correct because flowing glacier ice widens and deepens valleys, producing broad floors and steep sides.

questions.question: In Earth's continental crust, temperature generally increases with depth according to what term?
questions.explanation: Geothermal gradient is correct because it describes the increase in temperature with increasing depth inside Earth.

questions.question: Which sedimentary rock forms primarily through the evaporation of saline water and commonly contains the mineral halite?
questions.explanation: Rock salt is correct because it is an evaporite composed predominantly of halite deposited as saline water evaporates.

questions.question: The 21-centimeter line used to map neutral hydrogen in the Milky Way arises from which atomic transition?
questions.correctAnswer: The hyperfine spin-flip transition of neutral hydrogen's ground state
incorrectAnswers: The electronic transition from n = 2 to n = 1 in neutral hydrogen
The vibrational transition of molecular hydrogen
The ionization of neutral hydrogen by ultraviolet photons
questions.explanation: The hyperfine spin-flip transition of neutral hydrogen's ground state produces the 21-centimeter radio line, because the proton and electron spins change from parallel to antiparallel.

questions.question: In the hydrogen Lyman-alpha line, which transition occurs?
questions.correctAnswer: An electron transitions from n = 2 to n = 1
incorrectAnswers: An electron transitions from n = 3 to n = 2
An electron transitions from n = 1 to n = 2
An electron transitions from n = 4 to n = 1
questions.explanation: An electron transitions from n = 2 to n = 1 in the Lyman-alpha line, which is the first-line transition of the hydrogen Lyman series.

questions.question: What physical mechanism primarily supports a white dwarf against gravitational collapse?
incorrectAnswers: Thermal gas pressure from hydrogen fusion
questions.explanation: Electron degeneracy pressure supports a white dwarf because its electrons obey the Pauli exclusion principle and resist being compressed into identical quantum states.

questions.question: The Galilean moons Io, Europa, and Ganymede participate in which orbital-resonance relationship?
questions.explanation: A 1:2:4 orbital-period resonance describes the Laplace resonance: for every orbit of Ganymede, Europa makes two and Io makes four.

questions.question: What is the principal atmospheric constituent of Titan?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is Titan's principal atmospheric constituent, making up most of its dense atmosphere; methane is present in a much smaller abundance.

questions.question: Pluto is trapped in what mean-motion resonance with Neptune?
questions.explanation: A 3:2 resonance means Pluto completes two orbits while Neptune completes three, preventing close encounters despite Pluto's orbit crossing Neptune's orbital distance.

questions.question: What is the primary nuclear reaction chain powering the Sun?
questions.explanation: The proton–proton chain is the Sun's primary energy-producing reaction sequence, fusing hydrogen nuclei into helium.

questions.question: What observable quantity is directly determined by the depth of a transiting exoplanet's light curve, under the simplest geometric approximation?
questions.explanation: The squared planet-to-star radius ratio determines the transit depth because the blocked fraction of stellar disk area is approximately (Rp/Rs)².

questions.question: In the radial-velocity method of exoplanet detection, what produces the measured periodic spectral-line shifts?
questions.correctAnswer: The star's motion around the system's center of mass
incorrectAnswers: The planet's reflected light changing color
The star's rotation around its own axis alone
questions.explanation: The star's motion around the system's center of mass causes periodic Doppler shifts in its spectral lines, revealing the gravitational influence of an orbiting planet.

questions.question: What type of object is the compact remnant left by a core-collapse supernova when its mass is insufficient to form a black hole?
questions.explanation: A neutron star is the compact remnant formed when a massive star's collapsed core is supported primarily by neutron degeneracy and nuclear forces rather than becoming a black hole.

questions.question: What is the defining physical cause of a pulsar's regular radio pulses?
questions.correctAnswer: A rotating, magnetized neutron star whose emission beam sweeps across Earth
incorrectAnswers: Periodic nuclear fusion flashes on a white dwarf
Orbital eclipses of a star by an asteroid belt
Radial pulsations of a red giant's entire atmosphere
questions.explanation: A rotating, magnetized neutron star whose emission beam sweeps across Earth produces pulsar pulses, analogous to a lighthouse beam.

questions.question: What kind of supernova is conventionally associated with the thermonuclear disruption of a carbon–oxygen white dwarf?
questions.explanation: Type Ia supernova describes the thermonuclear disruption of a carbon–oxygen white dwarf, producing a characteristic spectrum without hydrogen lines.

questions.question: Which effect allows astronomers to infer the presence of unseen mass from the distortion of background-galaxy images?
questions.explanation: Gravitational lensing bends and magnifies light from background galaxies through the intervening mass's spacetime curvature, allowing that mass to be studied even when it is unseen.

questions.question: What is the main physical origin of the seasons on Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Earth's axial tilt relative to its orbital plane
incorrectAnswers: Earth's varying distance from the Sun alone
Changes in the Sun's rotation rate
questions.explanation: Earth's axial tilt relative to its orbital plane causes the seasons by changing each hemisphere's solar illumination angle and daylight duration during the orbit.

questions.question: What type of rotational state does the Moon exhibit, causing the same lunar hemisphere to face Earth continually?
questions.explanation: Synchronous rotation means the Moon's rotation period equals its orbital period, so the same hemisphere continually faces Earth.

questions.question: Which spectral classification describes the Sun?
questions.explanation: G2V is the Sun's spectral classification: G2 denotes its spectral type and subclass, while V denotes a main-sequence luminosity class.

questions.question: What does the luminosity class V signify in a stellar spectral classification such as G2V?
questions.explanation: Main-sequence star is what luminosity class V signifies; such stars are sustained primarily by hydrogen fusion in their cores.

questions.question: Which process creates elements heavier than iron through successive neutron captures followed by beta decay on relatively long timescales?
questions.explanation: The s-process creates many elements heavier than iron through slow neutron captures, with beta decay occurring between captures when necessary.

questions.question: What is the defining boundary of a black hole known as the event horizon?
questions.correctAnswer: The boundary beyond which no future-directed light signal can reach a distant observer
incorrectAnswers: The surface where matter becomes solid neutronium
The radius at which the black hole's temperature becomes zero
The boundary of the accretion disk's outer edge
questions.explanation: The boundary beyond which no future-directed light signal can reach a distant observer is the event horizon, which marks the causal limit of a black hole.

questions.question: What does the Chandrasekhar limit describe in stellar astrophysics?
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum mass of a cold, nonrotating white dwarf supported by electron degeneracy pressure
incorrectAnswers: The minimum mass required for hydrogen fusion in a star
The maximum mass of a neutron star before any collapse
The mass at which a protostar first becomes optically visible
questions.explanation: The maximum mass of a cold, nonrotating white dwarf supported by electron degeneracy pressure is the Chandrasekhar limit; above it, that support cannot prevent further collapse.

questions.question: In which city is the Eiffel Tower located?
questions.explanation: Paris is correct because the Eiffel Tower stands in Paris, France.

questions.question: The Nile River flows into which body of water?
questions.explanation: Mediterranean Sea is correct because the Nile empties into the Mediterranean Sea on Egypt's northern coast.

questions.question: Machu Picchu is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Peru is correct because Machu Picchu is an Inca site in the Peruvian Andes.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: Australia is correct because the Great Barrier Reef extends along the northeastern coast of Australia.

questions.question: On which continent is the Sahara Desert located?
questions.explanation: Africa is correct because the Sahara covers much of northern Africa.

questions.question: Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Venezuela is correct because Angel Falls is located in Venezuela's Canaima National Park.

questions.question: Mount Fuji is located on which island nation?
questions.explanation: Japan is correct because Mount Fuji is a prominent volcano on Japan's Honshu Island.

questions.question: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic Ocean with which other ocean?
questions.explanation: Pacific Ocean is correct because the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

questions.question: Petra, the ancient rock-cut city, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Jordan is correct because Petra is an archaeological city in southern Jordan.

questions.question: Lake Baikal is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Russia is correct because Lake Baikal lies in the Russian region of Siberia.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal is located in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: Agra is correct because the Taj Mahal stands on the Yamuna River in Agra, India.

questions.question: The Danube River empties into which sea?
questions.explanation: Black Sea is correct because the Danube forms a delta on the Black Sea coast.

questions.question: The Andes mountain range runs primarily along which side of South America?
questions.explanation: Western side is correct because the Andes extend along the western edge of South America.

questions.question: Victoria Falls is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Zambezi River is correct because Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River.

questions.question: The Acropolis is a famous historic landmark in which city?
questions.explanation: Athens is correct because the Acropolis is an ancient citadel overlooking Athens, Greece.

questions.question: The Galápagos Islands belong to which country?
questions.explanation: Ecuador is correct because the Galápagos Islands are an Ecuadorian archipelago in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: The Burj Khalifa is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Dubai is correct because the Burj Khalifa is a landmark skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

questions.question: Iguazu Falls lies on the border between Brazil and which other country?
questions.explanation: Argentina is correct because Iguazu Falls is shared by Brazil and Argentina.

questions.question: Uluru, also known as Ayers Rock, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Australia is correct because Uluru is a large sandstone formation in central Australia.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe from which continent?
questions.explanation: Africa is correct because the Strait of Gibraltar separates southern Spain in Europe from northern Africa.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Middlemarch?
questions.explanation: George Eliot is the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, who wrote Middlemarch.

questions.question: The Odyssey is traditionally attributed to which author?
questions.explanation: Homer is the traditional author of The Odyssey, an ancient Greek epic poem.

questions.question: Who wrote the poem The Waste Land?
questions.explanation: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land, first published in 1922.

questions.question: What is the subtitle of Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein?
questions.explanation: The novel's full title is Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, so the correctAnswer is The Modern Prometheus.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Things Fall Apart?
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe wrote Things Fall Apart, a novel centered on Okonkwo and Igbo society.

questions.question: Who wrote The Divine Comedy?
questions.explanation: Dante Alighieri wrote The Divine Comedy, which includes Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso.

questions.question: In Geoffrey Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales, what destination are the pilgrims traveling toward?
questions.explanation: The pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales are traveling to Canterbury Cathedral, so the correctAnswer is Canterbury.

questions.question: What is the surname of the heroine Elizabeth in Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth Bennet is the central character of Pride and Prejudice, so the correctAnswer is Bennet.

questions.question: What is the name of the fictional town in Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude?
questions.explanation: Macondo is the fictional town in which much of One Hundred Years of Solitude takes place.

questions.question: Beowulf was composed in which language?
questions.explanation: Beowulf is an Old English epic poem, making Old English the correctAnswer.

questions.question: Who wrote The Picture of Dorian Gray?
questions.explanation: Oscar Wilde wrote The Picture of Dorian Gray, his only novel.

questions.question: In which poetic form is John Milton's Paradise Lost written?
questions.explanation: Paradise Lost is written in blank verse, consisting primarily of unrhymed iambic pentameter.

questions.question: Who wrote Don Quixote?
questions.explanation: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, first published in two parts in the early seventeenth century.

questions.question: Who is traditionally credited with writing The Tale of Genji?
questions.explanation: Murasaki Shikibu is traditionally credited with writing The Tale of Genji.

questions.question: What is the name of the protagonist in Franz Kafka's The Metamorphosis?
questions.explanation: Gregor Samsa is the protagonist who awakens transformed in The Metamorphosis.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Mrs Dalloway?
questions.explanation: Virginia Woolf wrote Mrs Dalloway, a novel focused on a single day in Clarissa Dalloway's life.

questions.question: In Oscar Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, what is Jack Worthing's invented name in the city?
questions.explanation: Jack Worthing uses the invented name Ernest while in the city, so the correctAnswer is Ernest.

questions.question: Who wrote the essay-length work A Room of One's Own?
questions.explanation: Virginia Woolf wrote A Room of One's Own, a work examining women, fiction, and material independence.

questions.question: What is the name of the old fisherman in Ernest Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea?
questions.explanation: Santiago is the elderly fisherman at the center of The Old Man and the Sea.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek sculptor is traditionally credited with formulating the canon of proportions exemplified by the Doryphoros?
questions.explanation: Polykleitos is correct because ancient literary sources associate him with a proportional canon and with the Doryphoros.

questions.question: The Narmer Palette is generally interpreted as commemorating the unification of which political entities?

questions.explanation: Miso is a traditional fermented paste made primarily from soybeans, salt, and koji culture.

questions.question: Which ancient Roman fermented fish sauce was commonly used as a seasoning?
questions.explanation: Garum was an ancient Roman fish sauce made by fermenting fish, salt, and related ingredients, and it was widely used as a seasoning.

questions.question: Which enzyme catalyzes the first major step of carbon fixation in the Calvin cycle of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: RuBisCO is correct because it catalyzes the fixation of carbon dioxide to ribulose bisphosphate in the Calvin cycle.

questions.question: Which plant tissue transports water and dissolved mineral nutrients primarily from roots toward shoots?
questions.explanation: Xylem is correct because it conducts water and mineral ions from the roots through the plant, mainly toward the shoots.

questions.question: Which plant hormone promotes stomatal closure during water stress?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid is correct because it promotes stomatal closure and helps plants conserve water during drought stress.

questions.question: In legumes, which organisms commonly form root nodules that fix atmospheric nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria is correct because these bacteria live symbiotically in legume root nodules and convert atmospheric nitrogen into usable nitrogen compounds.

questions.question: What is the primary function of phloem in vascular plants?
questions.correctAnswer: Transporting sugars and other organic compounds
questions.explanation: Transporting sugars and other organic compounds is correct because phloem distributes photosynthetic products, especially sucrose, throughout the plant.

questions.question: What type of symbiotic association exists between a fungus and the roots of a plant in a mycorrhiza?
questions.explanation: Mutualism is correct because mycorrhizal fungi generally receive carbohydrates from the plant while improving the plant's access to water and mineral nutrients.

questions.question: What organisms form the photosynthetic partner in most lichens?
questions.explanation: Algae or cyanobacteria is correct because the photosynthetic partner of a lichen is typically a green alga or a cyanobacterium living with a fungus.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of C4 photosynthesis compared with C3 photosynthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: Initial carbon fixation occurs in four-carbon compounds
questions.explanation: Initial carbon fixation occurs in four-carbon compounds is correct because C4 plants first incorporate carbon dioxide into four-carbon molecules before the Calvin cycle.

questions.question: Which specialized root structures enable many mangrove species to obtain oxygen in waterlogged soils?
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores is correct because these aerial roots project above oxygen-poor soil or water and facilitate gas exchange.

questions.question: What process disperses seeds when they are carried externally on the bodies of animals?
questions.explanation: Epizoochory is correct because it is the dispersal of seeds or fruits attached to the outside of an animal's body.

questions.question: What is a keystone species?
questions.correctAnswer: A species with a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance
incorrectAnswers: The most abundant species in every ecosystem
A species found only in deserts
A species that produces no offspring
questions.explanation: A species with a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance is correct because this is the defining ecological meaning of keystone species.

questions.question: What is biomagnification?
questions.correctAnswer: The increase in concentration of a persistent substance at higher trophic levels
incorrectAnswers: The breakdown of rocks by roots
The increase of oxygen during photosynthesis
The movement of water through xylem
questions.explanation: The increase in concentration of a persistent substance at higher trophic levels is correct because predators can accumulate greater concentrations of substances such as certain mercury compounds.

questions.question: In ecological succession, what type of succession begins on a surface lacking soil, such as newly exposed bare rock?
questions.explanation: Primary succession is correct because it begins where soil has not previously formed, such as on newly exposed rock.

questions.question: Which interaction benefits both participating species?
questions.explanation: Mutualism is correct because both species gain a benefit from the interaction.

questions.question: What is a trophic cascade?
questions.correctAnswer: A chain of indirect effects across multiple trophic levels caused by changes at one level
incorrectAnswers: The seasonal migration of one species
The conversion of sunlight directly into nitrogen
The formation of a single-species population
questions.explanation: A chain of indirect effects across multiple trophic levels caused by changes at one level is correct because changes in predators or other consumers can propagate through an ecosystem.

questions.question: Which group of mammals is characterized by laying eggs rather than giving birth to live young?
questions.explanation: Monotremes is correct because this mammalian group, which includes the platypus and echidnas, lays eggs.

questions.question: Which animals use echolocation as a primary means of detecting objects and prey?
questions.explanation: Toothed whales is correct because dolphins, porpoises, and other toothed whales emit sounds and interpret returning echoes to navigate and locate prey.

questions.question: What physiological mechanism helps many fish extract oxygen efficiently from water as it passes over their gills?
questions.explanation: Countercurrent exchange is correct because blood and water flow in opposite directions across the gills, maintaining a diffusion gradient for oxygen along much of the exchange surface.

questions.question: Which symbiotic organisms provide most reef-building corals with photosynthetically produced energy?
questions.explanation: Dinoflagellate algae is correct because photosynthetic dinoflagellates living in coral tissues supply the coral with much of its photosynthetic energy.

questions.question: What term describes a species introduced outside its native range that causes ecological or economic harm?
questions.explanation: Invasive species is correct because the term refers to a non-native organism whose spread causes harmful ecological, economic, or health effects.

questions.question: In Egyptian mythology, which deity is traditionally depicted recording the result of the weighing of the deceased person's heart against the feather of Ma'at?
questions.explanation: Thoth is correct because Egyptian funerary scenes commonly depict him recording the outcome of the heart-weighing judgment. Anubis conducts the weighing, Osiris presides over the judgment, and Horus is associated with kingship and protection.

questions.question: In the Popol Vuh, which pair of brothers are the Hero Twins who defeat the lords of Xibalba?
questions.explanation: Hunahpu and Xbalanque are correct because they are the Hero Twins who undergo trials in Xibalba and ultimately overcome its rulers in the Popol Vuh.

questions.question: According to the Kojiki, which Japanese deity was born from Izanagi's left eye during his purification after visiting Yomi?
questions.explanation: Amaterasu is correct because the Kojiki says she emerged from Izanagi's left eye. Tsukuyomi emerged from his right eye, and Susanoo from his nose.

questions.question: In the Finnish Kalevala, which character forges the magical Sampo?
questions.explanation: Ilmarinen is correct because the Kalevala identifies him as the divine smith who forges the Sampo. Väinämöinen is a sage and singer, while Lemminkäinen and Joukahainen have different roles.

questions.question: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, what is the name of the survivor of the great flood who tells Gilgamesh how he attained immortality?
questions.explanation: Utnapishtim is correct because he is the flood survivor who recounts his story to Gilgamesh and was granted eternal life by the gods. Enkidu, Shamash, and Humbaba are different figures.

questions.question: In Irish mythology, what was Cú Chulainn's childhood name?
questions.explanation: Sétanta is correct because Cú Chulainn was known by that name before acquiring his better-known heroic name after killing Culann's hound.

questions.question: In Zoroastrian tradition, which figure is the destructive spirit opposed to Ahura Mazda?
questions.explanation: Angra Mainyu is correct because he is the destructive spirit, also called Ahriman, opposed to the beneficent order associated with Ahura Mazda. Mithra, Vohu Manah, and Atar have different functions.

questions.question: In the Shahnameh, what is the name of Rostam's famous horse?
questions.explanation: Rakhsh is correct because he is Rostam's extraordinary horse in the Shahnameh. Shabdiz belongs to the Persian king Khusrau, while Buraq is an Islamic tradition's heavenly mount.

questions.question: In Greek mythology, who was the mother of Achilles?
questions.explanation: Thetis is correct because Achilles was the son of the sea-nymph Thetis and the mortal Peleus. Hera, Leto, and Eurydice are not his mother.

questions.question: In the Mahabharata, who serves as Arjuna's charioteer during the battle of Kurukshetra?
questions.explanation: Krishna is correct because he serves as Arjuna's charioteer and delivers the Bhagavad Gita during the Kurukshetra war. Bhishma, Drona, and Yudhishthira are other major figures in the epic.

questions.question: In Chinese mythology, which figure is traditionally credited with creating humanity from yellow earth?
questions.explanation: Nüwa is correct because Chinese creation myths describe her molding humans from yellow earth. Chang'e is associated with the Moon, Xiwangmu with the Queen Mother of the West, and Leizu with sericulture.

questions.question: In Inuit mythology, which figure is associated with ruling over marine animals from beneath the sea?
questions.explanation: Sedna is correct because Inuit traditions portray her as the powerful undersea figure who controls marine animals. Amaterasu, Pele, and Baba Yaga belong to other mythological traditions.

questions.question: In Yoruba mythology, which orisha is especially associated with iron, warfare, and metalworking?
questions.explanation: Ogun is correct because he is the Yoruba orisha associated with iron, tools, warfare, and metalworking. Eshu, Yemaya, and Obatala have different domains.

questions.question: In Māori mythology, what landmass is said to have been fished up by Māui?
questions.correctAnswer: Te Ika-a-Māui, the North Island of New Zealand
incorrectAnswers: The South Island of New Zealand
questions.explanation: Te Ika-a-Māui, the North Island of New Zealand is correct because its traditional Māori name means 'the fish of Māui,' referring to the island's mythical fishing from the sea.

questions.question: In Slavic folklore, what object is traditionally said to contain Koschei the Deathless's death?
questions.correctAnswer: A needle inside an egg inside a duck inside a hare inside an iron chest
incorrectAnswers: A ring hidden beneath a stone
A sword buried under a mountain
A mirror kept in a silver tower
questions.explanation: A needle inside an egg inside a duck inside a hare inside an iron chest is correct because this nested chain is the traditional hiding place of Koschei's death in versions of the tale.

questions.question: In Japanese folklore, what kind of creature is a kappa?
questions.explanation: A water-dwelling yokai is correct because the kappa is a Japanese water spirit or yokai, commonly depicted with a water-filled depression on its head.

questions.question: In West African and African-diaspora folklore, which animal is most characteristically associated with the trickster figure Anansi?
questions.explanation: Spider is correct because Anansi is traditionally portrayed as a spider trickster and storyteller, especially in Akan traditions. Tortoise and hare are trickster figures in other traditions, but they are not Anansi's characteristic form.

questions.question: In Arthurian legend, what is the name of the magician and prophet who serves as King Arthur's adviser?
questions.explanation: Merlin is correct because he is the magician and prophetic adviser associated with Arthur's rise and reign. Gawain, Kay, and Bedivere are knights or companions rather than Arthur's magician adviser.

questions.question: In Greek mythology, which Titan is specifically associated with bearing the heavens on his shoulders?
questions.explanation: Atlas is correct because Zeus condemned him to support the heavens after the Titanomachy. Cronus, Hyperion, and Coeus are other Titans without this defining punishment.

questions.question: In Hawaiian mythology, which goddess is traditionally associated with volcanoes and the active volcano Kīlauea?
questions.explanation: Pele is correct because Hawaiian tradition identifies her as the goddess of volcanoes and associates her especially with Kīlauea. Hina, Haumea, and Namaka have distinct mythological identities.

questions.question: Which philosophical method is associated with Socrates and uses persistent questioning to examine beliefs?
questions.explanation: The Socratic method is correct because Socrates is traditionally associated with examining ideas through disciplined questioning.

questions.question: What school of philosophy was founded by Plato in Athens?
questions.explanation: The Academy is correct because Plato founded this philosophical school in Athens.

questions.question: According to Aristotle, what is the virtuous balance between two extremes called?
questions.explanation: The golden mean is correct because Aristotle described virtue as a balanced position between extremes.

questions.question: Which philosopher wrote the statement “I think, therefore I am”?
questions.explanation: René Descartes is correct because he presented “I think, therefore I am” as a foundational statement in his philosophy.

questions.question: What principle in utilitarianism says that actions should promote the greatest overall happiness?
questions.explanation: The greatest happiness principle is correct because utilitarianism evaluates actions by their contribution to overall happiness or well-being.

questions.question: What name did Immanuel Kant give to the unconditional moral command that applies to all rational beings?
questions.explanation: The categorical imperative is correct because Kant used this term for an unconditional moral requirement.

questions.question: Which philosophical view holds that knowledge is primarily gained through sensory experience?
questions.explanation: Empiricism is correct because it emphasizes observation and sensory experience as major sources of knowledge.

questions.question: Which philosophical view emphasizes reason as a primary source of knowledge?
questions.explanation: Rationalism is correct because it gives reason a central role in acquiring knowledge.

questions.question: Which ancient philosophical school teaches that virtue is the only true good and that people should focus on what they can control?
questions.explanation: Stoicism is correct because Stoic philosophy identifies virtue as the highest good and distinguishes controllable from uncontrollable events.

questions.question: Who founded the philosophical school of Epicureanism?
questions.explanation: Epicurus is correct because he founded Epicureanism in Athens.

questions.question: In Plato’s Republic, what does the allegory of the cave primarily illustrate?
questions.correctAnswer: The movement from ignorance to knowledge
questions.explanation: The movement from ignorance to knowledge is correct because Plato’s cave allegory represents education and the ascent toward understanding.

questions.question: Which philosopher is traditionally regarded as the founder of formal logic through his study of syllogisms?
questions.explanation: Aristotle is correct because his analysis of syllogisms established a foundational system of formal logic.

questions.question: In Confucian philosophy, what term refers to filial piety, or respect and duty toward one’s parents?
questions.explanation: Xiao is correct because it is the Confucian term for filial piety and devotion to one’s parents.

questions.question: Which ancient Chinese philosopher is traditionally associated with writing the Tao Te Ching?
questions.explanation: Laozi is correct because tradition attributes the Tao Te Ching to him.

questions.question: In Buddhism, what term refers to the unsatisfactoriness or suffering that characterizes ordinary existence?
questions.explanation: Dukkha is correct because it is the Buddhist term for suffering, dissatisfaction, or unsatisfactoriness.

questions.question: In the Bhagavad Gita, who gives philosophical guidance to Arjuna?
questions.explanation: Krishna is correct because he instructs Arjuna on duty, action, and spiritual knowledge in the Bhagavad Gita.

questions.question: Who wrote Leviathan, a major work of social and political philosophy?
questions.explanation: Thomas Hobbes is correct because he wrote Leviathan, which presents his influential account of political authority and the social contract.

questions.question: Which philosopher wrote Being and Nothingness?
questions.explanation: Jean-Paul Sartre is correct because he wrote Being and Nothingness, a major work of existentialist philosophy.

questions.question: Which philosopher is most closely associated with the idea that a scientific claim must be falsifiable?
questions.explanation: Karl Popper is correct because he proposed falsifiability as a key criterion for distinguishing scientific theories from non-scientific claims.

questions.question: What philosophical position holds that moral values and objective meaning do not exist?
questions.explanation: Nihilism is correct because it is the philosophical position commonly associated with the denial of objective meaning or values.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone contains the same decree written in which three scripts?
questions.correctAnswer: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Ancient Greek
questions.explanation: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Ancient Greek are the three scripts used for the decree on the Rosetta Stone, enabling the decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs.

questions.question: The Great Bath, one of the best-known structures of the Indus Valley Civilization, was discovered at which site?
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-daro contains the Great Bath, a large, carefully constructed brick structure from the Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.question: Which archaeologist is credited with deciphering the Mycenaean script Linear B?
questions.explanation: Michael Ventris deciphered Linear B in the early 1950s and demonstrated that it records an early form of Greek.

questions.question: Who founded the Akkadian Empire in Mesopotamia?
questions.explanation: Sargon of Akkad founded the Akkadian Empire during the third millennium BCE and ruled from the city of Akkad.

questions.question: Petra, famous for its rock-cut architecture, was the principal city of which ancient people?
questions.explanation: The Nabataeans established Petra as their major political and commercial center in the region of modern Jordan.

questions.question: The palace complex at Knossos is most closely associated with which ancient civilization?
questions.explanation: The Minoans built the palace complex at Knossos on Crete, a major archaeological site of Bronze Age Aegean civilization.

questions.question: The monumental carved heads found at sites such as San Lorenzo and La Venta are characteristic of which civilization?
questions.explanation: The Olmec civilization is especially known for its large basalt colossal heads discovered at major Gulf Coast sites.

questions.question: Which Achaemenid Persian ruler ordered the construction of the Royal Road linking Susa and Sardis?
questions.explanation: Darius I organized and improved the Royal Road between Susa and Sardis as part of the Achaemenid imperial communications system.

questions.question: The Antikythera mechanism is generally interpreted as an ancient device used primarily to calculate what?
questions.explanation: Astronomical cycles and positions were calculated by the Antikythera mechanism, a complex Hellenistic-era geared device recovered from a shipwreck.

questions.question: The Hittite capital of Hattusa was located in which modern country?
questions.explanation: Turkey is the modern country where the ruins of Hattusa, the capital of the Hittite Empire, are located.

questions.question: What is the name of the Mesoamerican calendrical system that records dates by counting days from a fixed starting point?
questions.explanation: The Maya Long Count records elapsed days from a fixed creation-era starting date, allowing dates to be expressed over long periods.

questions.question: What material added to Roman concrete helped it set in underwater conditions?
questions.explanation: Volcanic ash, especially pozzolanic ash, reacted with lime and enabled Roman concrete to harden effectively, including in underwater structures.

questions.question: Which ancient writing system was used by the Mycenaeans to record an early form of Greek?
questions.explanation: Linear B was used by the Mycenaeans for administrative records and represents an early form of the Greek language.

questions.question: The Standard of Ur was excavated from a royal cemetery at which ancient Mesopotamian city?
questions.explanation: Ur is the city whose Royal Cemetery produced the artifact now called the Standard of Ur.

questions.question: Which city served as a major capital of the Kingdom of Kush during its later period?
questions.explanation: Meroë served as a major capital of Kush and is known archaeologically for its royal cemeteries and distinctive pyramids.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the city of Teotihuacan?
questions.explanation: The Teotihuacan civilization built the monumental city of Teotihuacan in central Mexico; its original builders are not identified by a surviving historical name.

questions.question: Who piloted the first nonstop solo transatlantic flight, completed in 1927 from New York to Paris?
questions.explanation: Charles Lindbergh piloted the first nonstop solo transatlantic flight in the aircraft Spirit of St. Louis in May 1927.

questions.question: Who completed the first circumnavigation of Earth after taking command of the expedition begun by Ferdinand Magellan?
questions.explanation: Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the first circumnavigation in 1522 after Magellan was killed in the Philippines.

questions.question: Which explorer led the first expedition to reach the geographic South Pole?
questions.explanation: Roald Amundsen led the Norwegian expedition that reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911.

questions.question: Who led the first successful maritime transit of the Northwest Passage, completed during the voyage of the Gjøa?
questions.explanation: Roald Amundsen led the Gjøa expedition, which completed the first successful maritime transit of the Northwest Passage from 1903 to 1906.

questions.question: What was the name of the first artificial satellite placed into Earth orbit?
questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957.

questions.question: Which spacecraft carried Yuri Gagarin during the first human spaceflight?
questions.explanation: Vostok 1 carried Yuri Gagarin on 12 April 1961, making him the first human to orbit Earth.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963.

questions.question: Which Portuguese navigator first rounded the Cape of Good Hope from the Atlantic Ocean in 1488?
questions.explanation: Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, demonstrating a sea route around the southern tip of Africa.

questions.question: Who commanded the first Portuguese voyage to reach India by sailing around the Cape of Good Hope?
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama commanded the expedition that reached Calicut, India, by sea in 1498 via the route around Africa.

questions.question: What was the name of the winter encampment where the Lewis and Clark Expedition stayed near the Pacific coast in 1805–1806?
questions.explanation: Fort Clatsop was the expedition's winter encampment near the mouth of the Columbia River from December 1805 to March 1806.

questions.question: Who led the 1947 Kon-Tiki expedition across the Pacific Ocean on a balsa-wood raft?
questions.explanation: Thor Heyerdahl led the Kon-Tiki expedition from Peru to the Tuamotu Archipelago to test a theory about possible pre-Columbian oceanic contact.

questions.question: What was the name of the bathyscaphe that carried Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh to the Challenger Deep in 1960?
questions.explanation: Trieste carried Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh to the Challenger Deep on 23 January 1960, the first crewed descent to that depth.

questions.question: At what location was the ceremonial “golden spike” driven to mark completion of the first U.S. transcontinental railroad in 1869?
questions.explanation: Promontory Summit in Utah was where the Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads were joined on 10 May 1869.

questions.question: What was the first locomotive to enter the Rainhill Trials in 1829 and win the competition?
questions.explanation: Rocket, designed by George and Robert Stephenson, won the Rainhill Trials in 1829 and demonstrated its suitability for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway.

questions.question: What was the name of the first commercial jet airliner to enter scheduled passenger service?
questions.explanation: The de Havilland Comet became the first commercial jet airliner in scheduled passenger service when it entered service in 1952.

questions.question: Which ship made the first official transit of the Panama Canal after its completion in 1914?
questions.explanation: SS Ancon made the first official transit of the Panama Canal on 15 August 1914.

questions.question: Who led the Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition, which completed the first overland crossing of Antarctica in 1958?
questions.explanation: Vivian Fuchs led the Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition, which crossed Antarctica overland from the Weddell Sea to the Ross Sea in 1957–1958.

questions.question: Who was the leader of the expedition that made the first recorded ascent of Annapurna I in 1950?
questions.explanation: Maurice Herzog led the French expedition that made the first ascent of Annapurna I, with Herzog and Louis Lachenal reaching the summit on 3 June 1950.

questions.question: Under which Ming emperor were the major treasure voyages of Zheng He initiated?
questions.explanation: The Yongle Emperor initiated Zheng He's major treasure voyages, which began in 1405 during the Ming dynasty.

questions.question: What is Nowruz traditionally celebrated as?
questions.explanation: The Persian New Year is correct because Nowruz is the traditional Persian New Year celebration marking the beginning of spring.

questions.question: What does the Japanese tradition of hanami involve?
questions.explanation: Viewing cherry blossoms is correct because hanami is the Japanese custom of enjoying the seasonal bloom of cherry trees.

questions.question: What is a kimono?
questions.explanation: A traditional Japanese garment is correct because a kimono is a distinctive robe-like item of Japanese clothing.

questions.question: The haka is traditionally associated with which Indigenous people?
questions.explanation: The Māori of New Zealand is correct because the haka is a traditional Māori performance involving vigorous movement, chanting, and singing.

questions.question: What is a kilt traditionally associated with?
questions.explanation: Scotland is correct because the kilt is a traditional Scottish garment, especially associated with Highland dress.

questions.question: What is a sari?
questions.explanation: A traditional South Asian garment is correct because a sari is a long piece of fabric worn as clothing in South Asia.

questions.question: Ramadan is which month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The ninth month is correct because Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.

questions.question: What is Holi widely known as?
incorrectAnswers: The Jewish festival of unleavened bread
questions.explanation: The Hindu festival of colors is correct because Holi is a major Hindu celebration known for the use of colored powders and dyes.

questions.question: Diwali is commonly known by what description?
questions.explanation: The festival of lights is correct because Diwali is widely called the festival of lights and is celebrated with lamps and other lights.

questions.question: What is kente traditionally associated with?
questions.explanation: Ghana is correct because kente is a brightly woven textile traditionally associated with Ghana, especially Akan peoples.

questions.question: What traditional textile technique is Indonesia especially known for?
questions.explanation: Batik is correct because Indonesian batik uses wax-resist methods to create patterned fabrics.

questions.question: What is a gamelan?
questions.explanation: An Indonesian musical ensemble is correct because gamelan is an ensemble featuring instruments such as gongs and metallophones in Indonesia.

questions.question: Kabuki is a traditional form of theater from which country?
questions.explanation: Japan is correct because kabuki is a traditional Japanese theater form known for stylized acting, costumes, and makeup.

questions.question: Fado is a traditional musical genre from which country?
questions.explanation: Portugal is correct because fado is a traditional Portuguese music genre, especially associated with expressive singing.

questions.question: What is wayang kulit?
questions.explanation: Indonesian shadow-puppet theater is correct because wayang kulit uses leather puppets whose silhouettes are projected onto a screen.

questions.question: What is mehndi?
questions.explanation: Decorative henna body art is correct because mehndi is the South Asian tradition of applying temporary designs with henna.

questions.question: Capoeira combines martial-arts movements with which other cultural form?
questions.explanation: Dance and music is correct because capoeira is a Brazilian cultural practice combining martial-arts movements, dance, music, and singing.

questions.question: What is injera?
questions.explanation: A traditional Ethiopian flatbread is correct because injera is a spongy, fermented flatbread central to Ethiopian cuisine.

questions.question: What is mate traditionally consumed as?
questions.explanation: A South American herbal infusion is correct because mate is a caffeinated drink prepared by steeping yerba mate leaves.

questions.question: Inti Raymi was an Inca festival dedicated to which deity?
questions.explanation: The sun god is correct because Inti Raymi was an Inca festival honoring Inti, the Inca sun deity.

questions.question: In economics, what term denotes the value of the next-best alternative forgone when a choice is made?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative forgone when a decision is made.

questions.question: According to the theory of comparative advantage, a country should specialize in producing goods for which it has what?
questions.explanation: The lower opportunity cost determines comparative advantage, even when one country is more productive in producing every good.

questions.question: Which characteristic distinguishes a pure public good from a private good?
questions.correctAnswer: It is both non-rivalrous and non-excludable
incorrectAnswers: It is produced only by governments
questions.explanation: It is both non-rivalrous and non-excludable: one person’s use does not reduce availability to others, and people cannot readily be excluded from using it.

questions.question: What is an externality in economics?
questions.correctAnswer: A cost or benefit imposed on a third party outside a transaction
incorrectAnswers: A tax imposed on imported goods
A change in a firm’s internal accounting method
A payment made directly to a government employee
questions.explanation: A cost or benefit imposed on a third party outside a transaction is an externality because it affects people not directly involved in the exchange.

questions.question: Which graphical tool represents the distribution of income or wealth across a population?
questions.explanation: Lorenz curve represents the cumulative distribution of income or wealth across a population.

questions.question: What does the Consumer Price Index primarily measure?
questions.correctAnswer: Changes in the prices of a basket of consumer goods and services
incorrectAnswers: Changes in the value of a country’s exports only
questions.explanation: Changes in the prices of a basket of consumer goods and services are what the Consumer Price Index measures.

questions.question: Gross domestic product differs from gross national product because GDP measures production based primarily on what?
questions.correctAnswer: The geographic territory where production occurs
incorrectAnswers: The ownership of all financial assets
The number of households in the country
questions.explanation: The geographic territory where production occurs is the basis of GDP, whereas GNP is based on the income or production of a nation’s residents and nationals.

questions.question: When a central bank buys government securities in an open-market operation, what is the usual immediate monetary effect?
incorrectAnswers: It eliminates all commercial bank lending
It fixes the exchange rate permanently
questions.explanation: It increases the money supply because the central bank pays sellers, adding reserves to the banking system.

questions.question: Who wrote The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, published in 1936?
questions.explanation: John Maynard Keynes wrote The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, published in 1936.

questions.question: What does the price elasticity of demand measure?
questions.correctAnswer: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price
incorrectAnswers: The responsiveness of supply to a change in income
The total value of goods produced by a firm
The change in tax revenue caused by inflation
questions.explanation: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price is what price elasticity of demand measures.

questions.question: Which sociologist developed the typology of traditional, charismatic, and rational-legal authority?
questions.explanation: Max Weber developed the typology of traditional, charismatic, and rational-legal authority.

questions.question: Which sociologist wrote Suicide, a classic study linking patterns of suicide to forms of social integration and regulation?
questions.explanation: Émile Durkheim wrote Suicide, analyzing how social integration and regulation relate to suicide rates.

questions.question: Which anthropologist is especially associated with establishing participant observation through his fieldwork in the Trobriand Islands?
questions.explanation: Bronisław Malinowski is especially associated with establishing participant observation through his Trobriand Islands fieldwork.

questions.question: Who authored The Social Contract, first published in French in 1762?
questions.explanation: Jean-Jacques Rousseau authored The Social Contract, which was first published in French in 1762.

questions.question: In sociology, what term did Émile Durkheim use for a condition of weakened or unclear social norms?
questions.explanation: Anomie is the term Émile Durkheim used for a condition in which social norms are weakened or unclear.

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency is the middle value when a data set is arranged in numerical order?
questions.explanation: Median is the middle value when a data set is arranged in numerical order.

questions.question: In Marxist theory, what are the means of production?
questions.correctAnswer: The resources and institutions used to produce goods and services
incorrectAnswers: Only the wages paid to workers
questions.explanation: The resources and institutions used to produce goods and services are the means of production in Marxist theory.

questions.question: Who introduced the term cognitive dissonance for the discomfort caused by inconsistent beliefs or behavior?
questions.explanation: Leon Festinger introduced the term cognitive dissonance for discomfort caused by inconsistent beliefs or behavior.

questions.question: Which sociologist coined the term primary group for intimate, enduring groups such as families and close friendship circles?
questions.explanation: Charles Horton Cooley coined the term primary group for intimate, enduring groups such as families and close friendship circles.

questions.question: Which rules, first published in 1867, introduced mandatory gloves, three-minute rounds, and the prohibition of wrestling in modern boxing?
questions.explanation: The Marquess of Queensberry Rules is correct because these rules were published in 1867 and reshaped professional boxing.

questions.question: Which organization introduced the penalty kick into association football's Laws of the Game in 1891?
questions.explanation: The International Football Association Board is correct because it approved the penalty kick as a new law in 1891.

questions.question: At which ground was the first officially recognized international association-football match played in 1872?
questions.explanation: Hamilton Crescent is correct because Scotland and England played the first officially recognized international match there in 1872.

questions.question: Which club won the first Football Association Challenge Cup final in 1872?
questions.explanation: Wanderers is correct because they defeated the Royal Engineers 1–0 in the inaugural FA Cup final in 1872.

questions.question: Which team won the first Test cricket match, played against England at Melbourne in 1877?
questions.explanation: Australia is correct because Australia won the first recognized Test match by 45 runs at Melbourne in 1877.

questions.question: Which publication coined the term “The Ashes” in an 1882 obituary for English cricket?
questions.explanation: The Sporting Times is correct because its 1882 mock obituary said English cricket had died and that its ashes would be taken to Australia.

questions.question: Which team won the first modern World Series of Major League Baseball, held in 1903?
questions.explanation: Boston Americans is correct because they defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates in the 1903 World Series.

questions.question: At which Olympic Games was the modern five-ring Olympic flag first used?
questions.explanation: The 1920 Antwerp Games is correct because the Olympic flag was first used ceremonially at Antwerp in 1920.

questions.question: Which city hosted the first Winter Olympic Games in 1924?
questions.explanation: Chamonix is correct because it hosted the 1924 International Winter Sports Week, later recognized as the first Winter Olympic Games.

questions.question: In which city were the first officially recognized Paralympic Games held in 1960?
questions.explanation: Rome is correct because the first officially recognized Paralympic Games were held there in 1960.

questions.question: Which yacht won the first America's Cup race in 1851?
questions.explanation: America is correct because the schooner America won the 100 Guineas Cup race around the Isle of Wight in 1851.

questions.question: Which club was the first recipient of the Stanley Cup in 1893?
questions.explanation: Montreal Amateur Athletic Association is correct because its affiliated hockey team was awarded the first Stanley Cup in 1893.

questions.question: Who won the inaugural Tour de France in 1903?
questions.explanation: Maurice Garin is correct because he won the first Tour de France, held in 1903.

questions.question: Who won the first Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 1950?
questions.explanation: Giuseppe Farina is correct because he won the inaugural Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 1950.

questions.question: Which country won the inaugural Thomas Cup badminton competition in 1948–49?
questions.explanation: Malaya is correct because it defeated Denmark in the final of the first Thomas Cup competition.

questions.question: Who made the first officially recognized maximum break of 147 in snooker, in 1955?
questions.explanation: Joe Davis is correct because he compiled the first officially recognized 147 break in 1955 at Leicester Square Hall in London.

questions.question: In which ancient Greek city-state did democracy first develop?
questions.explanation: Athens developed the form of direct democracy for which it is historically known.

questions.question: Who became the first Roman emperor?
questions.explanation: Augustus became the first Roman emperor in 27 BCE after the end of the Roman Republic.

questions.question: Which Roman leader was assassinated on the Ides of March in 44 BCE?
questions.explanation: Julius Caesar was assassinated by Roman senators on March 15, 44 BCE, traditionally called the Ides of March.

questions.question: Which Persian king invaded Greece during the Greco-Persian Wars and fought at Thermopylae?
questions.explanation: Xerxes I led the Persian invasion of Greece in 480 BCE, including the campaign that involved the Battle of Thermopylae.

questions.question: Which ancient Indian emperor adopted Buddhism after the Battle of Kalinga?
questions.explanation: Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire embraced Buddhism after the devastating Battle of Kalinga.

questions.question: What writing system was used by the ancient Egyptians for monumental inscriptions?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphs were the formal pictorial writing system used by ancient Egyptians on temples, monuments, and other objects.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor founded Constantinople as a new imperial capital?
questions.explanation: Constantine I dedicated Constantinople in 330 CE as a major new capital of the Roman Empire.

questions.question: Who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066?
questions.explanation: William the Conqueror defeated Harold Godwinson at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

questions.question: Which Muslim leader recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187?
questions.explanation: Saladin recaptured Jerusalem after his victory over the Crusader army at the Battle of Hattin in 1187.

questions.question: Which Byzantine emperor commissioned the compilation known as the Justinian Code?
questions.explanation: Justinian I commissioned the systematic compilation of Roman law known as the Justinian Code.
